# The implementer makes Bash calls that set a search path, write a shell start file and print files that hold a key.
# The fake claude obeys --settings: the hook of the step runs `beehave check command` before each call and exits 2 on a listed kind.
# Each refused call is blocked and never ran, so the output violations stay empty.
# The two calls that read a named key pass the hook.
cp cmds-all cmds
cp flow/hit.star obey-hook
exec beehave run 7 --workflow flow/hit.star
stdout 'item 7 finished'

grep -count=1 '^blocked PATH=/tmp/x ls$' blocked.log
grep -count=1 '^blocked echo hi >> ~/.bashrc$' blocked.log
grep -count=1 '^blocked cat ~/.netrc$' blocked.log
grep -count=1 '^blocked git config --list$' blocked.log
grep -count=1 '^blocked printenv$' blocked.log
! grep 'git config --get' blocked.log
! grep 'printenv HOME' blocked.log
grep -count=5 '^blocked ' blocked.log

# Nothing ran, so the step records no violations and the audit sees an empty value.
! exists seen.log

-- cmds-all --
PATH=/tmp/x ls
echo hi >> ~/.bashrc
cat ~/.netrc
git config --list
printenv
git config --get user.name
printenv HOME
-- flow/hit.star --
def main(item):
    implement = agent(name = "implement", prompt = "prompts/implement.md", model = "sonnet", forbid_commands = ["env-override", "config-read"])
    agent(name = "audit", prompt = "prompts/audit.md", model = "sonnet", inputs = {"seen": implement.violations})
